title: Fabrication of a Crystalline Nanocellulose Embedded Agarose Biomaterial Ink for Bone Marrow-Derived Mast Cell Culture
protocol: Prepare complete RPMI-1640 culture medium by adding the supplements listed in Table 1 to the indicated final concentrations.
Adjust the pH of the medium to 7.4-7.6 using NaOH.
Filter-sterilize the medium using a single-use, bottle-top filter (0.2 µm pore size).
Store the prepared medium at 4 °C in the dark for up to 2 months.
Obtain femurs from mice in accordance with local animal care protocols.
Remove skin and muscle from the hip joint using scissors.
Gently twist the femur slightly to pull it out of the hip socket, being careful not to break off the femoral head.
Cut the tibia away from the femur at the medial fabella using scissors.
Remove the paw by cutting just above the calcaneum and discard.
Using a scalpel, remove skin and cartilage from the femur and tibia pieces.
Make a clean cut on each end of the femur and tibia with scissors to expose the red bone marrow.
Prepare a 26 G needle with a 5 mL luer-lock syringe and fill it with approximately 5 mL of complete media.
Holding the femur or tibia with forceps, insert the needle into one end of the bone.
Gently press the syringe to inject medium into the bone.
Hold the bone over a 50 mL sterile conical tube and gently inject approximately 5 mL of medium into the bone, applying some pressure.
Observe pieces of bone marrow falling out as thin red ribbons and into the conical tube.
Spin down the aspirates.
Resuspend the aspirates in complete medium or transfer them into a T175 cm² sterile tissue culture flask containing 50 mL of complete RPMI-1640 medium.
Maintain the cultures in complete RPMI-1640 medium supplemented with 30 ng/mL mouse recombinant interleukin (IL)-3.
Observe the cultures under a light microscope after 1 day.
Feed cell cultures by adding 15 mL of fresh medium every 3-5 days using the complete RPMI-1640 medium.
Spin down cells at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature once per week.
Resuspend the spun-down cells in fresh complete RPMI-1640 medium.
Split the cultures 1:4 into new T174 flasks containing 50 mL of fresh medium after one week.
Determine cell purity by measuring surface expression of CD117 (Kit) and FceRI receptors using flow cytometry after 4 weeks.
Maintain BMMCs with 20 ng/mL of IL-3 in complete RPMI-1640 medium starting from the fourth week.
Feed cultures every 3–5 days, pellet cells by centrifugation once per week, and resuspend them in fresh complete RPMI-1640 medium after six weeks when cell division ceases.
Add 0.2 g of agarose powder to PBS (final volume 10 mL) and boil for 1 min at 100 °C to dissolve.
Dissolve 2.5 g of CNC powder in PBS (final volume 10 mL) to prepare a 25% w/v mixture.
Dissolve 2 g of CNC powder in PBS (final volume 10 mL) to prepare a 20% w/v mixture, and serially dilute the 20% w/v mixture to prepare 10, 5, and 2% w/v CNC mixtures.
Heat the 25, 20, 10, 5, and 2% w/v CNC-PBS mixtures to 37 °C for 10 min.
Add 0.46 g of D-mannitol to the hot agarose solution (final volume 10 mL) and dissolve.

Mix the pre-warmed 25, 20, 10, 5, and 2% w/v CNC-PBS mixtures with the hot agarose/D-mannitol solution in a 1:1 ratio to yield final CNC concentrations of 12.5, 10, 5, 2.5, and 1% w/v in hydrogel mixtures.
Add 500 µL/well of above solutions prepared in step 2.6 in quadruplicate to a 24-well culture plate and let stand for 30 min at room temperature to facilitate polymerization.
Carefully layer 1000 µL of the BMMC suspension (density 1.1 × 10^6 cells/mL) on top of the hydrogel substrates with a micropipettor without touching the gel surface.
Incubate the BMMCs on the hydrogel substrates in a sterile incubator (5% CO2, humidified atmosphere) at 37 °C for 18 h.
Carefully remove the culture medium containing BMMCs from the top of the CNC/agarose/D-mannitol, avoiding the gel.
Transfer the cells into a 1.5 mL microfuge tube.
Wash the BMMCs twice with PBS (pH 7.4) containing 0.5% w/v bovine serum albumin at 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the washed cells in 180 µL of PBS-0.5% w/v BSA to a final density of 1.5 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a 96 well round-bottom plate.
Filter-sterilize all PBS-0.5% w/v BSA solutions twice using a 0.2 µm pore-size syringe filter, and store at 4 °C.
Add 20 µL of PBS-0.5% w/v BSA to the cells.
Prepare 10x PI (100 µg/mL) in PBS-0.5% w/v BSA, and add 20 µL to the cells for a final concentration of 10 µg/mL.
Incubate the cells with PBS-0.5% w/v BSA or PI solution for either 1 h at 4 °C or 15 min at room temperature in the dark.
Acquire fluorescence data using a flow cytometer equipped with an Argon ion laser (488-514 nm) and bandpass filter to enable detection of fluorescence emission at 578 nm.
Acquire 20,000 events per sample at a flow rate of 30 µL/min at room temperature.
Wash BMMCs twice with filtered PBS-0.5% BSA at 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend washed cells in 180 µL of PBS containing 0.5% w/v BSA to achieve a concentration of 1.5 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Transfer resuspended cells to a 96-well round-bottom plate.
Prepare 10x antibody working solutions in filter-sterilized PBS-0.5% w/v BSA.
Add 20 µL of the prepared 10x antibody working solution containing CD117 (c-Kit)-phycoerythrin (PE) to achieve a final concentration of 0.06 µg/mL.
Add 20 µL of the prepared 10x antibody working solution containing FcεRIα-allophycocyanin (APC) to achieve a final concentration of 0.06 µg/mL.
Prepare 10x isotype control working solutions in filter-sterilized PBS-0.5% w/v BSA.
Add 20 µL of the prepared 10x isotype control working solution containing rat IgG2b κ isotype control-PE to separate wells.
Add 20 µL of the prepared 10x isotype control working solution containing Armenian hamster IgG isotype control-APC to separate wells.
Incubate the 96-well round-bottom plate for 1 h at 4 °C in the dark.
Wash the cells by adding 200 µL of fresh PBS-0.5% w/v BSA buffer to each well.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Repeat the wash step once more.
Carefully remove the supernatant without touching the cell pellet.
Leave behind some supernatant to ensure that the cell pellet remains undisturbed.
After washing, resuspend cells in 100 µL of 0.5% w/v BSA, 0.05% w/v sodium azide in PBS (pH 7.4) that has been sterile-filtered twice with a 0.2 µm pore-size syringe filter.
Acquire fluorescence data in the PE and APC detector channels using a flow cytometer.
Plot forward scatter (FSC) along the x-axis and side scatter (SSC) along the y-axis.
Gate for the conserved cell population with a FSC range of log10 1.5-5.0 and an SSC range of log10 0.75-3.25 in the untreated and unstained cells.
Remove the blue end caps from the 3 mL biomaterial ink cartridge.
Affix a sterile 22 G (blue) conical bioprinting nozzle to the luer-lock end of the Bioink cartridge.
Connect the air pressure supply tubing for printhead 1 (PH1, left) to the opposite end of the cartridge.
Insert the cartridge with its attached conical bioprinting nozzle into the vertical slot of PH1.
Firmly seat the cartridge in PH1 with the conical bioprinting nozzle extending below the printhead.
Tighten the screw on PH1 clockwise until finger-tight to lock the Bioink cartridge in place.
Power on the 3D bioprinter.
Launch the bioprinter software on a PC connected to the 3D bioprinter via a USB 2.0 cable.
Click the CONNECT button to sync the software with the 3D bioprinter.
Select the PREPARE BIOPRINT option in the main control menu of the 3D bioprinter.
Scroll down to and select the HOME AXES option.
Remove a sterile 24-well culture plate from its sealed plastic wrapping.
Mark a dot on the center point of well D1 on the underside of the plate with a permanent marker.
Place the 24-well culture plate on the printbed with well D1 located at the front left corner of the printbed.
Select UTILITIES MENU and then select MOVE AXIS from the main control menu.
Move the printheads in 1 mm increments along the x- and y-axes until the conical bioprinting nozzle is directly over the dot marked under well D1.
Fine-tune the position of the conical bioprinting nozzle over the dot by moving the printheads in 0.1 mm increments if necessary.
Record the x- and y-coordinates of the conical bioprinting nozzle when directly over the center of well D1.
Raise the printbed in 1 mm increments until the bottom of well D1 is almost touching the conical bioprinting nozzle.
Fine-tune the movement of the printbed in 0.1 mm increments if necessary.
Select the Z-AXIS CALIBRATION option from the UTILITIES MENU.
Confirm the STORE Z CALIBRATION option.
Return to the main menu and select the PREPARE BIOPRINT option.
Scroll down to and select the CALIBRATE Z option.
Open the provided 24-well plate geometric code (G-code) file in the bioprinter software.
Update the x- and y-coordinates on Line 1 of the G-code file with new values.
Save the updated G-code file under a new name.
Connect the pneumatic pump tightly to the rear air intake port of the INKREDIBLE+ 3D bioprinter.
Turn on the pneumatic pump.
Pull out the forward control knob located on the right side of the INKREDIBLE+ 3D bioprinter.
Observe the digital pressure gauges for PH1 and PH2 located on the front of the bioprinter each read close to 0 kPa.
Slowly rotate the forward control knob clockwise until the pressure indicated on the left gauge for PH1 reaches 12 kPa.
Place a folded tissue paper or piece of waterproof, sealing film under the print nozzle of the installed cartridge, being careful not to touch the print nozzle.
From the main control menu on the 3D bioprinter, select PREPARE BIOPRINT.
Navigate to and select TURN ON PH1.
Note that the biomaterial ink starts to extrude from the print nozzle.
If necessary, increase the extrusion pressure by rotating the control knob clockwise until the biomaterial ink is extruded in a continuous filament, and record the new pressure setting.
Select TURN OFF PH1 to stop extrusion of the biomaterial ink.
Remove the tissue paper or film containing the extruded biomaterial ink from the printbed.
Close the bioprinter door.
From the main control menu on the 3D bioprinter, select UTILITIES MENU.
Navigate to and select DISABLE SD PRINT.
Click on the LOAD button in the bioprinter software.
Select the updated 24-well plate G-code file saved in step 4.6.2.
In the right-hand control panel, select the PRINT PREVIEW tab.
Click on the PRINT button to commence bioprinting in well D1.
Cover the 24-well plate with its lid after printing completion.
Move the covered plate to a class II biosafety cabinet.
Immerse each rectilinear construct in two drops of sterile 50 mM CaCl2 solution.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Aspirate the CaCl2 solution from each construct carefully.
Rinse each construct once with 1 mL of 1x PBS (pH 7.4).
Maintain the 3D bioprinted rectilinear constructs in fresh 1x PBS until BMMCs are ready for seeding.
Seed aliquots of BMMCs onto the 3D bioprinted rectilinear scaffolds in triplicate for four different durations: 6, 18, 24, and 48 h.
Use BMMCs seeded into empty wells in triplicate for the same durations as untreated controls.
Aseptically transfer BMMCs from a T175 cm² culture flask to a sterile 50 mL conical tube.
Pellet the BMMCs at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the pellet in 50 mL of fresh complete RPMI medium containing 20 ng/mL of IL-3.
Calculate the live cell density by counting an aliquot of trypan blue-stained BMMCs using a hemacytometer.
Prepare a 6 mL aliquot of the BMMC suspension at a final density of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Aspirate PBS from wells A1-3 containing the 3D bioprinted rectilinear hydrogel scaffolds.
Pipette 1 mL of BMMC (1 × 10^6 cells/mL) suspension into each well A1-3.
Pipette 1 mL of BMMC (1 × 10^6 cells/mL) suspension into wells A4-6 without bioprinted constructs as untreated controls.
Incubate remaining wells containing bioprinted scaffolds (B1-3, C1-3, D1-3) in RPMI without additives to prevent dehydration.
Fill the wells without bioprinted scaffolds (B4-6, C4-6, D4-6) with 1 mL of PBS until appropriate time for seeding BMMCs.
Incubate the 24-well plate at 37 °C in a 5% CO2 humidified atmosphere.
For the 24 h incubation setup, aspirate pre-existing culture medium/buffer from wells B1-6.
Seed 1 mL of BMMC (1 × 10^6 cells/mL) suspension into these wells B1-6.
Return the plate to the incubator for 24 h incubation.
For the 18 h incubation setup, aspirate pre-existing culture medium/buffer from wells C1-6.
Seed 1 mL of BMMC (1 × 10^6 cells/mL) suspension into these wells C1-6.
Return the plate to the incubator for 18 h incubation.
Aspirate pre-existing culture medium/buffer from wells D1-6.
Seed 1 mL of BMMC (1 × 10^6 cells/mL) suspension into these wells.
Return the plate to the incubator.
Thoroughly resuspend the BMMCs in the culture medium within each well.
Transfer 40 µL of the homogeneous BMMC suspension from each well to sterile 1.5 mL microfuge tubes containing 760 µL of fresh complete RPMI medium.
Vortex briefly to mix the contents of the microfuge tubes.
Dispense 100 µL of the diluted BMMC suspensions in triplicate into a flat-bottom 96-well microtiter plate suitable for recording absorbance measurements.
Dispense 50 µL of XTT working solution to each well containing the BMMC cell suspension using a multichannel micropipette.
Incubate the 96-well plate at 37 °C in a 5% CO2 humidified atmosphere for 24 h.
Remove the 96-well plate from the incubator and allow to cool to room temperature.
Record absorbance values on a microplate spectrophotometer at 450 nm with background subtraction at 650 nm.
Transfer 960 µL of BMMC suspensions from each well of the 24-well plate to microfuge tubes.
Pellet the cells at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Pipette three 100 µL aliquots of cell culture supernatant from each microfuge tube into a 96-well microtiter flat-bottom plate.
Discard leftover supernatants and retain BMMC pellets for further staining with PI.
Pipette 50 µL of the LDH working solution into each 100 µL aliquot of supernatant.
Incubate in the dark at room temperature for 1 h.
Pipette 50 µL of 1 M acetic acid to each well to stop the reaction.
Record absorbance values on a microplate spectrophotometer at 490 nm with background subtraction at 680 nm.
Resuspend BMMC pellets in flow wash buffer (PBS [pH 7.4] containing 0.5% w/v BSA).
Pellet the cells at 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Repeat the wash step with flow wash buffer once more.
Resuspend each BMMC pellet in 400 μL of flow wash buffer.
Pipette 20 µL of flow wash buffer into wells A1-12 and B1-12 of a round-bottom 96-well microtiter plate.
Pipette 20 µL of 10x PI staining solution (100 µg/mL PI in flow wash buffer) into wells C1-12 and D1-12 of the same microtiter plate.
Dispense 180 μL of BMMC samples incubated on bioprinted hydrogel substrates into wells A1-12, one sample per well.
Dispense 180 μL of BMMC samples incubated without bioprinted hydrogel substrates into wells B1-12, one sample per well.
Use the BMMC samples in wells A1-12 and B1-12 as unstained controls for each treatment condition.
Dispense 180 μL of BMMC samples incubated on bioprinted constructs into wells C1-12, one sample per well.
Dispense 180 μL of BMMC samples incubated without bioprinted constructs into wells D1-12, one sample per well.
Incubate the plate either for 1 h at 4 °C or 15 min at room temperature in the dark.
Analyze the samples directly from the microtiter plate on a flow cytometer as previously described.
